MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  October 15, 2012

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7 p.m. on Monday, October
15, 2012, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Mayor Gazeley led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Estrada, Savidan, Traina, and Mayor Gazeley. Councilmember Sanchez was absent. Also
present were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin,
Community Services Director McPherron, Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and
Recreation Director Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. PRESENTATIONS

Presentation from Dr. Richard Vladovic, LAUSD Boardmember, relative to school matters.

Dr. Richard Vladovic introduced Dr. James Noble, Administrator of Operations, and Dr. Robert
Bravo, Instructional Superintendent, both newly appointed by the Los Angeles Unified School
District (LAUSD) - South Division. Dr. Vladovic talked about the high level of education in
Lomita schools, in which most of the schools were meeting or exceeding state academic
performance goals. According to Dr. Vladovic, overall the school district has done very well, in
spite of the budget cuts and difficult financial times, but he was concerned with the upcoming
election, which could potentially result in even more budget cuts for the school district.

Dr. Noble, Administrator of Operations, and Dr. Bravo, Instructional Superintendent, both talked
about their responsibilities with the (LAUSD) – South Division. For further questions, both Dr.
Noble and Dr. Bravo can be reached at 310-354-3400.

3. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Mayor Gazeley noted that staff had received a request from Councilmember Sanchez, who was
not able to attend the meeting, requesting that Item #8 be continued to a future meeting in order

  Page 1 of 5
 for him to participate in the discussion. Councilmember Traina moved to approve the agenda.
Mayor Gazeley seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:
Ayes: Councilmembers Estrada, Traina, Savidan, and Mayor Gazeley
Absent: Councilmember Sanchez

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed City Council that CERT training, which consists of five four-hour
classes, is now being required for all full-time staff.

City Manager Rock reported that he attended a legislative briefing breakfast held by the South
Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG), in which the topics for discussion included:
federal budget sequestration issues, federal grants, and excise taxes (specifically related to
gasoline). City Manager Rock mentioned that during the discussions it was stated that the
desire of the state government is to increase Vehicle License Fee (VLF), which would be used
for basic public works projects and the maintenance of streets, instead of increasing excise
taxes that have not been raised since 1990. According to City Manager Rock, U.S.
Congresswoman Maxine Waters was also present at the SBCCOG meeting.

City Manager Rock also stated that some State Senators had expressed their concerns over the
loss of sales tax in California when larger companies and airlines purchase their fuel in other
states.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina stated that the street lights, which were reported to be fixed at the
previous meeting, were still not operational, along with some other street lights in Lomita;
Councilmember Traina requested staff to follow-up on the matter. Public Works Director
Damasse responded that staff had placed an order for the repair through CalTrans, and added
that staff will provide a status update regarding street light repairs at a later date.

Councilmember Traina asked City Council to consider changing the procedure of how Council-
requested items are placed on a future City Council agenda. According to Councilmember
Traina, Councilmembers should be able to bring forward matters for discussion that would not
require staff to prepare staff reports for the items. Councilmember Traina suggested rethinking
the policy for placing items on the agenda, and perhaps setting up certain parameters, such as
possibly limiting the number of items per Councilmember per meeting or month. City Manager
Rock stated that the entire City Council would need to be present for such a discussion, and he
suggested bringing the topic up at a later date when the full Council is present.

Mayor Gazeley informed those in attendance that the City of Lomita had received a Certificate
of Achievement from the Government Finance Officers Association for its preparation of a
Comprehensive Financial Report. According to Mayor Gazeley, the certificate was issued to
Administrative Services Director Chavez; Mayor Gazeley congratulated her and the staff for this
recognition.

  Page 2 of 5
 6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, agreed with Councilmember Traina that City Councilmembers
should have the ability to bring forward items for discussion. Mr. McGrath also provided some
information and ideas regarding a possible dog park, which were based on his internet search.
According to Mr. McGrath, many cities have dog parks that require no cost to the City, but rather
utilize associations, grants, and other resources.

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, agreed with Mr. McGrath and Councilmember Traina that
citizens should be able to discuss issues in this forum. Also, Ms. Segawa asked staff to look
into the traffic signal on 252nd and Narbonne, as it takes a long time for the signal to change.
Furthermore, Ms. Segawa stated that in her last water bill, she was surprised to see that her
water consumption doubled; Ms. Segawa was concerned since there was no water leak, nor did
her family increase their water consumption. Ms. Segawa expressed her dissatisfaction that
she did not receive any response after she left a message regarding this issue.

Michael Pucci, Assistant Area Director of Public Affairs at Kaiser Permanente, and Board
Member of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, thanked Councilmembers for attending Chamber
of Commerce events, and invited everyone to the next Business Mixer, which is scheduled for
November 29, 2012, at 5 p.m., at Kaiser Medical Center.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, suggested that staff should look into installing day-glow green
pylon signs at the crosswalks.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Estrada moved to approve the Consent Agenda.  Councilmember Traina
seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:
Ayes: Councilmembers Estrada, Traina, Savidan, and Mayor Gazeley
Absent: Councilmember Sanchez

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting held on
  October 1, 2012, and Adjourned City Council Meeting held on October 1, 2012.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  d. Award of a Public Works Agreement to FS Construction for the Citywide Sidewalk and
  Pedestrian Safety Improvements Project in the amount of $216,649, and approve a total
  project budget of $249,164 (which includes a 15% contingency). RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  e. Renewal of Agreement with City of Inglewood for Parking Citation Processing Services.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
  Page 3 of 5
   PUBLIC HEARING

8. INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE RELATING TO AMENDMENT OF SALE OF
  ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES - ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2012-03 AND
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 279

This item was continued to the City Council Meeting scheduled for November 5, 2012.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

9. Discussion and direction to staff regarding placing recycling containers at City parks.

Parks and Recreation Director Harding stated that on September 17, 2012, City Council directed
staff to look into placing recycling containers at City parks. In response to that direction, staff's
recommendation is to initiate a pilot recycling program at Lomita Park and Hathaway Park in
order to ensure that the program operates smoothly, prior to expanding the program to all City
parks. According to Director Harding, the cost for this new program would be covered through
grant funds received from CalRecycle’s City/County Payment Program, and existing Parks staff
would be responsible for emptying the recycling container in the parks.

Councilmember Estrada moved to approve placing recycling containers in the two parks in order
to initiate the pilot recycle program. Councilmember Traina seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:
Ayes: Councilmembers Estrada, Traina, Savidan, and Mayor Gazeley
Absent: Councilmember Sanchez

10. Discussion and consideration of a Resolution establishing an Ad Hoc City Finance
  Committee.

City Manager Rock stated that the purpose of an Ad Hoc City Finance Committee would be for
the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem to work with staff on various finance items including a five-year
strategic financial plan, establishing a number of policies and procedures related to finance,
reviewing the annual operating and capital improvement budgets for Fiscal Year 2013-2014, and
working on improving the overall presentation of the budget by making it more user-friendly and
understandable.

Councilmember Traina commented that it would be beneficial for the entire City Council to be
part of the Finance Committee. City Manager Rock responded that the purpose of having a
subcommittee of two Councilmembers is so issues and technical information can be reviewed in
detail with recommendations presented to the entire City Council for discussion and approval.
In addition, according to City Manager Rock, with more than two Councilmembers on the
committee, the committee would be subject to the Brown Act, thereby requiring meetings to be
agendized. Councilmember Estrada moved to adopt the resolution establishing an Ad Hoc City
Finance Committee. Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:
Ayes: Councilmembers Estrada, Traina, Savidan, and Mayor Gazeley
  Page 4 of 5
 Absent: Councilmember Sanchez

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:50 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
